evaluation_target.rationale: The hazard describes the hazardous event as the vehicle suddenly stopping without an obstacle in front, and SG-3 states that the system shall prevent unintended braking.

phenomenon_of_interest.statement: Vehicle braking behavior in the described straight-ahead urban driving situation, including whether braking occurs and whether it is intended or unintended.
phenomenon_of_interest.scope: Straight ahead drive on a less frequented urban road with 50 km/h, without visible obstacles or vehicles in front of the ego vehicle, in good weather conditions.
phenomenon_of_interest.rationale: Evaluating prevention of unintended braking requires characterising braking behaviour within the operational situation in which the hazard is defined.

distinctions.contrast_a: The vehicle brakes as intended to avoid an obstacle or other justified collision-avoidance situation.
distinctions.contrast_b: The vehicle brakes unexpectedly / unintentionally when no obstacle is in front of the vehicle.
distinctions.rationale: The hazard explicitly contrasts a sudden stop without an obstacle against normal braking to avoid collisions, and collapsing these would lose the ability to determine whether the safety goal is violated.

orrs.obligation: An admissible observable representation must preserve whether braking is intended or unintended in the declared operational situation.
orrs.distinguishability_criterion: The representation must make intended braking and unintended braking distinguishable as different classes of braking outcome.
